plan.notes: Source: official University of Montana Academic Catalog, 2026-2027 edition (live catalog verified at https://catalog.umt.edu/ on 2026-09-30), 'Bachelor of Science - Computer Science; Algorithm Design Concentration' page: https://catalog.umt.edu/colleges-schools-programs/science/computer-science/bs-computer-science-algorithm-design/ and its official print PDF (same path + bs-computer-science-algorithm-design.pdf). Transcribed verbatim from the catalog's official 'Four Year Plan' grid (HTML table + PDF text cross-checked); the plan grid carries an internal stamp 'Last updated Autumn 2024' and is unchanged in the current 2026-2027 edition. CREDENTIAL HONESTY: the UM catalog offers the BS in Computer Science ONLY with a concentration (Algorithm Design, Data Science, Software Engineering); there is no concentration-free BS Computer Science sequence. This file covers the Algorithm Design concentration and the major field names it exactly; it must not be presented as a generic/plain BS CS. Blank grid cells labeled from the PDF: Sophomore Autumn 4-5 cr = 'Lab Science seq I', Sophomore Spring 4-5 cr = 'Lab Science seq II', Junior Spring 3-5 cr = 'Science Elective', Junior/Senior 9 cr rows = 'CS Core Elective' (upper-division CSCI electives). CREDIT MODEL: the catalog's plan totals 119-124 hours; the UM baccalaureate requires 120 credits. Variable slots are modeled at their minimums (placement math 3, lab science sequences 4 each) except the Science Elective, taken as 4, so the plan totals exactly 120; a student on the all-minimum 119 path needs 1 additional credit. FOOTNOTES: (1) M 121 College Algebra is a preparatory course carrying NO degree credit — 'must be taken at this time to assure progression through degree'; students placing into M 122/M 151 earn credit. (2) M 162 (Applied Calculus) is not accepted for this concentration. M 225 is listed as a corequisite for CSCI 232 in the plan grid. CSCI 315E fulfills the upper-division (advanced) writing requirement. Senior-year elective math option (M 361/M 362/M 414/M 440/M 485/STAT 421) may be taken in place of one upper-division CS elective per the catalog. CS elective limits per catalog: at most 3 credits from each of research (CSCI 390/490), independent study (CSCI 392/492), learning assistant (CSCI 394), internship (CSCI 398/498); 6 credits total across those groups. Prereq arrays are empty because the official plan grid states only the M 225 corequisite note; no prereqs were invented. No courses, credits, or titles invented.
